keyFindingsEn: Initial requirements seemed simple but proved complex: natural language Q&A across 10 years of project data, fast response times, security (no external APIs), and support for specialized files like OrcaFlex simulations. The data was 1TB of files in a disorganized Azure folder.

The tech stack chosen was Ollama for local LLM execution, nomic-embed-text for embeddings (due to its quality on technical documents), and LlamaIndex for RAG orchestration (document indexing, embedding generation, vector DB storage and querying). Python was used, and the initial prototype worked well with minimal code.

The first major obstacle was memory exhaustion. Attempting to process actual documents with LlamaIndex caused the notebook to crash when trying to load gigabyte-sized simulation files and videos into memory. The solution was to add a filtering pipeline to exclude dozens of extensions like mp4, exe, zip, .sim, .dat, and backup files.

Problems persisted even after file filtering. Scanned PDFs with unextractable text, hundreds of MB CAD files, and encrypted documents blocked the pipeline. A file size limit was set, and exception handling was added to skip text extraction failures.

Indexing became a long-term project. The task was moved from a laptop to a Hetzner cloud VM, and it took 2-3 weeks of uninterrupted processing to complete. The total cost was 184 euros, which many commenters considered a small price to pay compared to the engineering time.

Chunking strategy significantly impacted search quality. Too large chunks mixed irrelevant content, while too small chunks lost context. Specialized formats like OrcaFlex files required separate processing as standard text parsers couldn't create meaningful chunks.

The ultimate lesson was that 'data preprocessing is everything.' RAG system quality is determined by *how* data is refined and ingested, not just by choosing a good embedding model or vector DB. The author reached this conclusion despite being new to RAG, and experienced practitioners agreed in the comments.
evidenceEn: The author’s conclusion that ‘data preprocessing is key’ resonated strongly with experienced RAG practitioners. One commenter shared their experience of spending a week building an ETL process to extract price information with 100% accuracy from a 20-page PDF, criticizing the approach of simply converting PDFs to markdown and throwing them into a vector DB as ‘absurd.’

A counterargument to the claim that ‘RAG is dead’ emerged. In response to the assertion that RAG becomes unnecessary as LLM context windows grow, one commenter pointed out that ‘even if the entire Lord of the Rings could fit in context, an entire law library or Wikipedia, or 451GB of data like this article, is still many times larger.’ Another commenter viewed RAG as ‘AI Lite’ or ‘AI adjacent’ technology, predicting that sufficiently large context windows could limit the deterministic nature of RAG and restrict LLM inference capabilities.

There was regret over not using re-ranking. One commenter noted, ‘You used a good embedding model but didn’t use a re-ranker, which is a shame. Using a re-ranker allows you to use a smaller, cheaper embedding model and even use smaller embedding vectors.’ Re-ranking is a technique where an LLM re-sorts candidate documents retrieved by vector search based on relevance.

Advanced opinions mentioned structured data preprocessing and ReAG (reasoning-based RAG). One commenter advised, ‘Instead of throwing unstructured data directly into a vector DB, basic preprocessing and labeling, and embedding with a different schema can greatly improve search quality and flexibility. Adding a memory knowledge graph can then leverage context that updates over time.’

An interesting perspective on the 184 euro VM cost also surfaced. The comment ‘184 euros is just pocket change for a project that involved 3 weeks of engineering effort’ received widespread agreement. A question also arose about RAG tools that operate with a single file without a backend like SQLite, indicating a desire for simpler RAG solutions.
howToApplyEn: If you’re building a RAG system based on internal documents for the first time, prioritize creating a data filtering pipeline over selecting an embedding model. Filtering out files that cannot be text-extracted or are meaningless—like mp4, exe, zip, backups, and simulation results—can prevent memory exhaustion and pipeline interruptions.

For rapid prototyping of a local LLM-powered RAG system, consider starting with Ollama + LlamaIndex + nomic-embed-text. This stack is good for creating prototypes with minimal code, but be sure to add file size limits and exception handling before ingesting real data.

If indexing a large document set takes weeks, plan to process it on a cloud VM like Hetzner from the start instead of a laptop. VM costs are negligible compared to engineering time, and it allows for uninterrupted, long-running execution.

To improve search quality, adding a re-ranking step to your pipeline may be more effective than switching embedding models. Vector search retrieves the top-K candidates, and the re-ranker re-scores them based on relevance to the query, allowing you to even use smaller, cheaper embedding models.

title: PISmith: Reinforcement Learning-based Red Teaming for Prompt Injection Defenses

ko.oneLiner: 강화학습으로 훈련된 공격 LLM이 최신 Prompt Injection 방어 기법을 모두 우회하며 공격 성공률 100%를 달성한다.
keyFindings: Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507를 공격 LLM으로 사용, 단 100개 샘플로 훈련해도 13개 벤치마크 전체에서 평균 ASR@10 1.0, ASR@1 0.87 달성 (최강 방어인 Meta-SecAlign-8B 대상)
표준 GRPO를 그냥 쓰면 강한 방어 앞에서 보상이 거의 0이라 Entropy Collapse(탐색 중단)가 일어나 학습이 멈춤 - PISmith는 이걸 두 가지 방법으로 해결
Adaptive Entropy Regularization: 현재 성공률이 낮을수록 엔트로피 보너스를 강하게 줘서 다양한 공격 패턴 탐색을 유지
Dynamic Advantage Weighting: 성공한 rollout이 드물수록 해당 gradient를 최대 5배 증폭해서 희귀한 성공 신호가 학습에 제대로 반영되게 함
GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4.1-nano, GPT-5-nano 같은 closed-source 모델도 공격 성공 (InjecAgent에서 GPT-5-nano 대상 ASR@10 1.0, ASR@1 0.95)
8개 방어 시스템 평가 결과, utility(정상 성능)를 유지하면서 PISmith를 막는 방어는 단 하나도 없었음 - 강한 방어는 정상 사용도 막아버림
howToApply: 자사 LLM 서비스에 Sandwich, Instructional 같은 간단한 방어만 적용 중이라면 PISmith 같은 adaptive 공격에 거의 무방비 상태임 - 방어 강도를 재평가해야 함
RAG 파이프라인에서 외부 문서를 LLM에 넣기 전에 DataSentinel이나 DataFilter 같은 filter-based 방어를 쓰는 경우, utility 손실(-8~19%)을 감수해도 PISmith ASR이 0.52~0.63 수준으로 여전히 높음 - 방어 자체가 근본 해결책이 아님을 인지해야 함
PISmith의 훈련 프롬프트 템플릿(논문 Appendix D.3)을 참고해서 '공식 업데이트인 척 하는 injection' 패턴을 자체 red teaming에 활용 가능 - 실제 공격 패턴을 미리 테스트해볼 수 있음

en.oneLinerEn: A reinforcement learning-trained adversarial LLM bypasses all state-of-the-art prompt injection defenses, achieving 100% attack success rate.
en.targetAudienceEn: Security developers applying prompt injection defenses to LLM-based agents or RAG systems, or teams wanting to systematically test the security vulnerabilities of their AI services.
keyFindingsEn: Using Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 as the attacking LLM, training with only 100 samples achieves an average ASR@10 of 1.0 and ASR@1 of 0.87 across 13 benchmarks (against Meta-SecAlign-8B, the strongest defense).
Standard GRPO yields near-zero rewards under strong defenses, leading to Entropy Collapse (exploration halts) – PISmith resolves this with two methods.
Adaptive Entropy Regularization: Strongly incentivizes exploration of diverse attack patterns by providing a higher entropy bonus when the current success rate is low.
Dynamic Advantage Weighting: Amplifies the gradient of rare successful rollouts by up to 5x, ensuring that infrequent success signals are properly reflected in learning.
Attacks also succeed against closed-source models like GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4.1-nano, and GPT-5-nano (InjecAgent achieves ASR@10 1.0 and ASR@1 0.95 against GPT-5-nano).
Evaluation of 8 defense systems reveals that none can maintain utility (normal performance) while blocking PISmith – strong defenses block legitimate use as well.
evidenceEn: PISmith ASR@1 average of 0.87 vs. next best RL-Hammer 0.48, and static attacks 0.04 against Meta-SecAlign-8B (average across 13 benchmarks).
On HotpotQA-Long, PISmith ASR@10/ASR@1 = 0.99/0.61, RL-Hammer 0.04/0.01 (over 15x difference).
Total queries: PISmith 32,000 vs. TAP 82,110, PAIR 74,460, Strategy 194,140 – achieving the highest attack success rate with the fewest queries.
Ablation: Vanilla GRPO ASR@1 0.05, adding entropy only 0.09, adding boost only 0.57, both (PISmith) 0.87
howToApplyEn: If your LLM service only applies simple defenses like Sandwich or Instructional, it is largely defenseless against adaptive attacks like PISmith – reassess your defense strength.

Using filter-based defenses like DataSentinel or DataFilter before inserting external documents into the LLM in a RAG pipeline results in a PISmith ASR of 0.52~0.63, still high despite utility loss (-8~19%) – recognize that defense alone is not a fundamental solution.

Leverage PISmith’s training prompt templates (paper Appendix D.3) to incorporate ‘injection disguised as official updates’ patterns into your own red teaming exercises – proactively test for real-world attack patterns.

title: Tiny-Critic RAG: Empowering Agentic Fallback with Parameter-Efficient Small Language Models

ko.oneLiner: 1.7B 소형 모델이 GPT-4o-mini 수준의 RAG 노이즈 필터링을 달성하며 비용 98%, 지연 94.6% 절감
keyFindings: 잘못된 검색 결과가 에이전트에 들어가면 할루시네이션뿐 아니라 불필요한 멀티홉 추론 루프와 중복 툴 호출로 TTFT(첫 토큰 응답 시간)와 비용이 폭발적으로 늘어남
Qwen3-1.7B를 LoRA(소수 파라미터만 학습하는 기법)로 파인튜닝해 '이 검색 결과 쓸 수 있나/없나'만 판단하는 초소형 라우터(Tiny-Critic)로 만듦
Constrained Decoding(출력 토큰을 pass/fail 두 개로만 제한)과 Non-Thinking Mode(CoT 생략)를 조합해 라우팅 자체를 42ms로 끝냄
판단 결과가 fail이면 MCP(Model Context Protocol)를 통해 Tavily Search 같은 폴백 툴을 호출해 깨끗한 컨텍스트를 다시 가져옴
Zero-shot Qwen3-1.7B는 FPR(오탐율)이 38.2%였지만, LoRA 학습 후 4.1%로 떨어짐 — 파인튜닝 없이는 라우터로 못 씀
howToApply: 기존 RAG 파이프라인의 LLM 평가자(GPT-4o-mini 등)를 Qwen3-1.7B + LoRA 라우터로 교체. 검색 결과와 쿼리를 concat해서 'pass'/'fail' 하나만 받도록 constrained decoding 설정.
fail 판정 시 MCP 툴 호출로 폴백 검색을 연결. Tavily나 자체 검색 API를 MCP 서버로 래핑해두면 에이전트 루프에 자연스럽게 끼워 넣을 수 있음.
학습 데이터는 Natural Questions + HotpotQA 기반 5,000쿼리, BGE-M3로 Hard Negative를 rank 10~20에서 샘플링하는 노이즈 주입 프로토콜을 그대로 적용해 도메인 특화 라우터를 만들 수 있음.

en.oneLinerEn: A 1.7B parameter model achieves GPT-4o-mini level RAG noise filtering, reducing costs by 98% and latency by 94.6%.
en.targetAudienceEn: Backend/AI engineers concerned about API costs and latency when using LLM-as-a-judge in RAG pipelines. Specifically, teams struggling with token waste caused by incorrect search results in ReAct agents.
keyFindingsEn: Incorrect search results lead to hallucinations, unnecessary multi-hop reasoning loops, and redundant tool calls, exponentially increasing TTFT (Time To First Token) and costs.

Qwen3-1.7B was fine-tuned using LoRA (a technique for training only a small number of parameters) to create a tiny router ('Tiny-Critic') that simply determines 'whether this search result is usable or not'.
Combining Constrained Decoding (limiting output tokens to only pass/fail) and Non-Thinking Mode (omitting CoT) completes routing in just 42ms.
If the judgment is 'fail', MCP (Model Context Protocol) is used to call a fallback tool like Tavily Search to retrieve a clean context.
Zero-shot Qwen3-1.7B had an FPR (False Positive Rate) of 38.2%, but dropped to 4.1% after LoRA training — fine-tuning is essential for use as a router.
evidenceEn: Routing F1-Score: Tiny-Critic 0.912 vs GPT-4o-mini(Heavy-CRAG) 0.934 — statistically equivalent.
Routing TTFT: Heavy-CRAG 785ms → Tiny-Critic 42ms, a 94.6% reduction.
Cost per 10k queries: Heavy-CRAG $3.00 → Tiny-Critic $0.06, a 98% reduction.
Faithfulness in a 45% noisy environment: Naive RAG 0.44 vs Tiny-Critic 0.86 (maintaining a level of 0.89 when there is no noise).
howToApplyEn: Replace the existing LLM evaluator (e.g., GPT-4o-mini) in your RAG pipeline with the Qwen3-1.7B + LoRA router. Configure constrained decoding to receive only 'pass'/'fail' for the concatenated search results and query.
Connect fallback search via MCP tool calls upon 'fail' determination. Wrapping Tavily or your own search API as an MCP server allows for seamless integration into the agent loop.
Leverage the same noise injection protocol (based on Natural Questions + HotpotQA with 5,000 queries and BGE-M3 for ranking Hard Negatives from 10-20) to create a domain-specific router.

title: Control Illusion: The Failure of Instruction Hierarchies in Large Language Models

ko.oneLiner: 프롬프트 주입 연구에서 System 프롬프트는 User 프롬프트보다 우선하지 않으며, '90% 전문가가 추천' 같은 사회적 권위 표현이 오히려 더 강하게 LLM을 지배한다.
keyFindings: System/User 프롬프트 분리가 실제로는 신뢰할 수 있는 우선순위 체계를 만들지 못함 — 6개 최신 LLM 모두 실패
단순한 포맷 충돌(영어 vs 프랑스어, 대문자 vs 소문자)에서도 System 지시를 따르는 비율이 9.6~45.8%에 불과함
'You must always follow this constraint' 같이 명시적 강조를 해도 GPT-4o 기준 최대 63.8%에 그쳐 신뢰할 수 없는 수준
모델이 충돌을 인식했다고 명시적으로 언급하는 비율(ECAR)이 0.1~20.3%로 매우 낮고, 인식해도 올바른 우선순위를 따르지 않는 경우가 많음
모든 모델이 공통적으로 소문자 선호, 더 많은 문장 선호, 키워드 회피 같은 내재적 편향을 보임 — 이는 학습 데이터 패턴에서 기인
'CEO 지시', 'Nature 논문 추천', '전문가 90% 동의' 같은 사회적 권위 프레이밍이 System/User 분리보다 훨씬 강한 우선순위 효과를 냄 (Qwen: 14.4% → 65.8%)
howToApply: System 프롬프트만 믿고 보안/제어 규칙을 설계하면 안 됨. 크리티컬한 제약은 System + User 양쪽에 모두 넣거나, 응답 후처리로 규칙 준수 여부를 검증하는 레이어를 추가해야 함
사용자에게 규칙을 따르도록 유도할 때 '90% 사용자가 이 형식을 선호합니다' 또는 'OpenAI 가이드라인에 따르면...' 같은 사회적 권위/컨센서스 프레이밍을 쓰면 단순 System 지시보다 효과적일 수 있음
에이전트 시스템에서 외부 사용자 입력이 운영자 규칙을 오버라이드하는 prompt injection 위험을 고려할 때, System 프롬프트만의 보호는 불충분하므로 입력을 데이터로 처리하는 구조적 접근(예: StruQ 방식)을 검토해야 함

en.oneLinerEn: Research reveals system prompts don't reliably override user prompts, and social proof cues—like '90% of experts recommend'—exert a stronger influence on LLMs. This highlights the limitations of relying solely on system prompts for control.
en.targetAudienceEn: Backend/AI developers building LLM-powered services who aim to control user behavior with system prompts, particularly those designing multi-tenant agents or chatbots where operator rules should take precedence over user input.
keyFindingsEn: System/User prompt separation doesn't create a dependable hierarchy in practice—all six recent LLMs tested failed to consistently prioritize system instructions.
Even simple formatting conflicts (English vs. French, uppercase vs. lowercase) resulted in system instruction adherence rates of only 9.6–45.8%.
Explicit emphasis like 'You must always follow this constraint' only achieved up to 63.8% compliance with GPT-4o, an unreliable level.
The rate at which models explicitly acknowledge conflicts (ECAR) is very low, ranging from 0.1–20.3%, and even when recognized, they often don't follow the correct priority.
All models exhibit inherent biases—such as a preference for lowercase, longer sentences, and keyword avoidance—likely stemming from patterns in their training data.

Social proof framing—like 'CEO directive,' 'Nature paper recommendation,' or '90% expert agreement’—demonstrates a much stronger prioritization effect than System/User separation (Qwen: 14.4% → 65.8%).
evidenceEn: Model performance is 74.8–90.8% with a single constraint, but system priority compliance plummets to an average of 9.6% (Qwen-7B) to 45.8% (GPT-4o-mini) in conflict situations.
Priority Adherence Rate (PAR) with social proof framing: GPT-4o-mini increased from System/User 47.5% to social consensus 77.8%, and Qwen-7B from 14.4% to 65.8%.
Larger model size doesn't guarantee better results: Llama-70B averaged 16.4% vs. Llama-8B at 10.1%, and GPT-4o at 40.8% vs. GPT-4o-mini at 45.8%.
Even when conflicts are explicitly recognized (ECAR), non-compliance after recognition (R3ac) was 53.8% for GPT-4o-mini, meaning recognition doesn't lead to resolution.
howToApplyEn: Don't rely solely on system prompts for security or control rules. For critical constraints, include them in both the System and User prompts, or add a post-processing layer to verify rule compliance.

When prompting users to follow rules, using social proof/consensus framing—like '90% of users prefer this format' or 'According to OpenAI guidelines...'—can be more effective than simple system instructions.

Considering the risk of prompt injection where external user input overrides operator rules in agent systems, system prompt protection alone is insufficient; explore structural approaches that treat input as data (e.g., the StruQ method).

title: Are Aligned Large Language Models Still Misaligned?

ko.oneLiner: 단일 기준(안전성만, 가치만)으로 튜닝한 LLM은 현실의 복합 상황에서 50% 이상을 오판한다.
keyFindings: GPT-4o, Claude-3.5-Sonnet, Gemini-1.5-Pro 모두 '가족 모임에서 음주 허용' 같은 질문에서 안전은 통과했지만 문화·가치 차원에서 misalign 발생
Safety만 특화 fine-tuning한 모델: Safety Coverage 97.6% 달성했지만 False Failure Rate이 50% 넘어 정상 응답도 절반 이상 틀린 것으로 판정
범용 정렬 모델(MARL-FOCAL, TRINITYX)이 Alignment Score 81%로 단일 차원 특화 모델(63~66%)보다 실전에서 훨씬 견고
Mistral-7B-Instruct로 분류 + Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct로 희소 도메인 증강한 382,424개 샘플·112개 도메인 데이터셋 SAVACU 공개
SimHash 기반 중복 제거가 임베딩 유사도 방식보다 cross-split 누수율 0.4% vs 2.2%로 훨씬 안전
오픈웨이트 모델(Gemma-7B, DeepSeek-7B)은 FFR 낮지만 Coverage도 낮아 '보수적이지만 둔감한' 패턴 — 배포하면 alignment가 과소 적용됨
howToApply: 단일 차원 벤치마크(안전성만 체크하는 레드팀 테스트 등)로 통과한 모델도 SAVACU의 Safety+Value+Cultural 교차 서브셋으로 재검증하면 숨겨진 misalign을 발견할 수 있다
안전성 특화 fine-tuning을 할 때 튜닝 후 문화·가치 차원의 FFR을 별도 측정하는 단계를 CI/CD 평가 파이프라인에 추가하면 '과잉 거부(spurious rejection)' 문제를 사전에 잡을 수 있다
글로벌 서비스라면 HHH(Helpful, Harmless, Honest) 범용 alignment 목표로 학습된 모델이 특정 도메인 파인튜닝 모델보다 문화·가치 충돌 상황에서 더 안전하다는 걸 의사결정 근거로 활용

en.oneLinerEn: LLMs tuned on a single criterion (safety only, value only) misjudge over 50% of cases in real-world, complex scenarios.
en.targetAudienceEn: ML engineers designing safety and ethical policies for LLM-based services, or building alignment evaluation pipelines. AI safety teams concerned about cultural appropriateness and bias in global services.
keyFindingsEn: GPT-4o, Claude-3.5-Sonnet, and Gemini-1.5-Pro all passed safety checks on questions like 'Is alcohol allowed at family gatherings?' but exhibited misalignment in cultural and value dimensions.
Models fine-tuned solely for safety achieved 97.6% Safety Coverage, but a False Failure Rate exceeding 50%, indicating over half of correct responses were flagged as incorrect.

General alignment models (MARL-FOCAL, TRINITYX) demonstrated significantly greater robustness in real-world scenarios, achieving an Alignment Score of 81% compared to 63-66% for single-dimension specialized models.
SAVACU, a dataset of 382,424 samples across 112 domains created by classifying with Mistral-7B-Instruct and augmenting sparse domains with Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, has been released.
SimHash-based deduplication proved significantly safer than embedding similarity, with a cross-split leakage rate of 0.4% versus 2.2%.
Open-weight models (Gemma-7B, DeepSeek-7B) exhibit low FFR but also low Coverage, resulting in a ‘conservative but insensitive’ pattern – deploying them can lead to under-application of alignment.
evidenceEn: Safety-specialized fine-tuning models: Coverage 97.6% but FFR >50%, Alignment Score 63-66% – numerically confirming the drawbacks of single-dimension optimization.
General alignment models (MARL-FOCAL, TRINITYX): Maintained a balance with Overall Alignment Score 81.0-81.6% and FFR ≈18%.
Mistral-7B classifier vs. human annotators: Accuracy difference of 2.8-3.2%, Macro-F1 of 0.80 – validating the reliability of automated classification.
SimHash (τ=10) Normalized Aggregate Score 0.83 vs. embedding similarity 0.58 – comparing deduplication quality.
howToApplyEn: Revalidate models that pass single-dimension benchmarks (like red-teaming tests focusing solely on safety) using SAVACU’s Safety+Value+Cultural cross-subset to uncover hidden misalignments.

Add a step to your CI/CD evaluation pipeline to separately measure False Failure Rate in cultural and value dimensions after safety-focused fine-tuning to proactively catch ‘spurious rejection’ issues.

Leverage the fact that models trained on general HHH (Helpful, Harmless, Honest) alignment goals are safer in cultural and value conflict situations than domain-specific fine-tuned models as a decision-making basis for global services.

title: PSA: Claude Code has two cache bugs that can silently 10-20x your API costs — here's the root cause and workarounds

ko.oneLiner: Claude Code 스탠드얼론 바이너리와 --resume 옵션의 캐시 버그 두 개가 API 비용을 10-20배 증가시킨다.
keyFindings: 버그 1: 스탠드얼론 바이너리에는 Anthropic의 커스텀 Bun 포크에 네이티브 레이어 문자열 치환 로직이 있는데, 대화 히스토리에 특정 sentinel 문자열이 포함되면 매 API 요청마다 메시지 내용이 바뀐다.
sentinel 문자열은 CC 소스 코드를 읽었거나, 빌링 관련 헤더를 언급했거나, CLAUDE.md 파일에 관련 내용이 있을 때 대화에 포함될 수 있다.
메시지 내용이 매번 달라지면 캐시 prefix(이전 대화를 캐시해서 재사용하는 기능)가 깨져서 매 요청마다 전체 토큰을 다시 과금한다.
버그 1 우회법: 스탠드얼론 바이너리 대신 `npx claude` 방식으로 실행하면 이 치환 로직을 거치지 않아서 캐시가 정상 동작한다.
버그 2: v2.1.69부터 --resume 옵션을 쓰면 항상 캐시 미스가 발생한다. deferred_tools_delta의 순서가 fresh session과 resumed session 사이에 달라지는 게 원인이다.
--resume 시 시스템 프롬프트만 캐시되고 전체 대화 히스토리는 매번 처음부터 다시 읽혀서, resume 요청 하나에 10-20배 비용이 발생할 수 있다.
howToApply: 지금 당장: Claude Code를 스탠드얼론 바이너리로 실행 중이라면 `npx @anthropic-ai/claude-code` 방식으로 바꿔라. CLAUDE.md에 빌링/소스코드 관련 내용이 있는 경우 특히 중요하다.
--resume을 자주 쓰는 자동화 스크립트가 있다면 v2.1.69 이전 버전으로 다운그레이드하거나, resume 없이 새 세션으로 시작하는 방식으로 임시 우회한다.
Claude API 비용이 갑자기 치솟았는데 원인을 모르겠다면, Claude Code 버전과 실행 방식(standalone vs npx), --resume 사용 여부를 먼저 확인한다.

en.oneLinerEn: Two bugs in the Claude Code standalone binary and the `--resume` option inflate API costs by 10-20x. The issues stem from string replacement logic and improper caching of conversation history.
en.targetAudienceEn: Developers using Claude Code via CLI or automation scripts, particularly those continuing conversations with `--resume` or storing significant content in CLAUDE.md.
keyFindingsEn: Bug 1: The standalone binary uses Anthropic’s custom Bun fork with native layer string replacement logic. When specific sentinel strings are present in the conversation history, the message content changes with each API request.
Sentinel strings can appear in conversations if the user has read the CC source code, mentioned billing-related headers, or has relevant content in their CLAUDE.md file.
Changing message content breaks the cache prefix (which reuses previous conversations), resulting in full token billing for each request.
Bug 1 workaround: Running Claude Code with `npx claude` bypasses this replacement logic, allowing the cache to function normally.
Bug 2: Starting with v2.1.69, the `--resume` option consistently causes cache misses due to differing order of `deferred_tools_delta` between fresh and resumed sessions.
When using `--resume`, only the system prompt is cached, and the entire conversation history is re-read each time, potentially increasing the cost of a resume request by 10-20x.
evidenceEn: Bug 2 is reported to consistently reproduce after v2.1.69 when using `--resume`. The entire conversation history, excluding the system prompt, is treated as a cache miss.
Both bugs are explicitly stated to potentially increase API costs by 10-20x, with longer conversations incurring greater losses.
Bug 1 is exclusive to the standalone binary and does not reproduce when running with `npx`.
howToApplyEn: Immediately: If you’re running Claude Code as a standalone binary, switch to `npx @anthropic-ai/claude-code`. This is especially important if your CLAUDE.md file contains billing or source code-related content.
If you rely on automation scripts that frequently use `--resume`, either downgrade to a version prior to v2.1.69 or temporarily work around the issue by starting new sessions without resuming.
If you notice a sudden spike in Claude API costs, first check your Claude Code version, execution method (standalone vs npx), and whether you’re using `--resume`.

title: Aligning Crowd-sourced Human Feedback for Reinforcement Learning on Code Generation by Large Language Models

ko.oneLiner: cRLHF 프레임워크가 여러 사람의 코드 라인 평가를 Bayesian 방식으로 합산해 별도 Reward Model 없이 LLM 코드 생성 품질을 높인다.
keyFindings: cRLHF: 여러 annotator가 코드 각 라인을 correct/wrong으로 평가하면, Bayesian inference로 합산해 reward score를 자동 계산 — 별도 Reward Model 학습 단계가 사라짐
Honeypot 질문(정답 미리 아는 문제)으로 각 annotator의 신뢰도 pi 값을 자동 측정해, 부정확한 피드백의 가중치를 낮추는 품질 필터링 내장
WizardCoder-15B, StarCoder2-15B, CodeLlama-13B/7B, DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B 등 17개 모델(최대 15B 파라미터)에 TRL + LoRA + PPO로 파인튜닝 적용
대형 모델일수록 cRLHF 효과가 더 뚜렷하고, 소형 모델(PolyCoder-160M 등)에서는 변화가 미미함
L1 정규화(스파스 정규화)를 써서 노이즈 많은 annotator를 자동으로 걸러내 과적합 방지
annotator 신뢰도 업데이트를 반복 방식 대신 정규화 로지스틱 회귀 최적화로도 처리 가능(one-shot 글로벌 추정)
howToApply: 코드 annotation 플랫폼 구축 시, 처음 N개 문제를 Honeypot(정답 공개 안 한 채 정답 알고 있는 문제)으로 설정해 annotator pi 값을 초기화하면 품질 낮은 참여자를 자동 필터링할 수 있다
TRL 라이브러리의 PPO Trainer + LoRA 조합으로 기존 코드 LLM을 파인튜닝할 때, reward model 대신 cRLHF의 aligned score(s = 정답 라인 수 / 전체 라인 수)를 reward 값으로 직접 주입할 수 있다
내부 코드 리뷰 데이터나 팀원 평가 결과가 있다면, 동일한 Bayesian aggregation 로직으로 여러 리뷰어 의견을 단일 reward 점수로 변환해 파인튜닝에 재활용할 수 있다

en.oneLinerEn: cRLHF leverages Bayesian aggregation of code line evaluations from multiple annotators to enhance LLM code generation quality without requiring a separate Reward Model.
en.targetAudienceEn: ML engineers aiming to apply RLHF to code generation models, particularly those seeking to utilize crowdsourced feedback without the cost of Reward Model training. This is relevant for teams internalizing tools like GitHub Copilot or fine-tuning domain-specific code LLMs.
keyFindingsEn: cRLHF: Reward scores are automatically calculated by aggregating correct/wrong evaluations of each code line from multiple annotators using Bayesian inference – eliminating the need for a separate Reward Model training step.

An inherent quality filter is built-in that automatically measures each annotator’s reliability (pi value) using honeypot questions (problems with known solutions), reducing the weight of inaccurate feedback.
Fine-tuning was applied to 17 models (up to 15B parameters) including WizardCoder-15B, StarCoder2-15B, CodeLlama-13B/7B, and DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B using TRL + LoRA + PPO.
The cRLHF effect is more pronounced in larger models, with minimal changes observed in smaller models (e.g., PolyCoder-160M).
L1 regularization (sparse regularization) is used to automatically filter noisy annotators and prevent overfitting.
Annotator reliability updates can also be handled through optimization with regularized logistic regression (one-shot global estimation) instead of iterative updates.
evidenceEn: Average across 17 models on the HumanEval benchmark: Pass@1 +0.2%, Pass@10 +0.3%, Pass@100 +1.2%
Average across 17 models on the MBPP benchmark: Pass@1 +0.2%, Pass@10 +0.6%, Pass@100 +0.6%
On HumanEval, 12 out of 17 models showed improvement in Pass@10, while on MBPP, 10 models showed simultaneous improvement in Pass@10 and Pass@100.
howToApplyEn: When building a code annotation platform, initializing annotator pi values with the first N problems as honeypots (problems with known solutions but not revealed) can automatically filter out low-quality participants.

When fine-tuning existing code LLMs with the TRL library’s PPO Trainer + LoRA combination, the aligned score from cRLHF (s = number of correct lines / total lines) can be directly injected as the reward value instead of a reward model.

Internal code review data or team member evaluation results can be repurposed for fine-tuning by converting multiple reviewer opinions into a single reward score using the same Bayesian aggregation logic.

title: You should write an agent

ko.oneLiner: LLM agent는 간단한 코드로 구현 가능하며, 직접 만들어봐야만 동작 원리를 정확히 이해하고 올바른 판단을 내릴 수 있다.
keyFindings: LLM agent의 핵심은 놀랍도록 단순하다. OpenAI API 호출 하나에 context 리스트를 관리하는 것만으로 ChatGPT와 동일한 대화형 앱을 15줄 안에 만들 수 있다.
흔히 복잡하게 느껴지는 'context window'는 사실 문자열 리스트에 불과하다. 사용자 입력과 LLM 응답을 리스트에 쌓아서 매번 통째로 보내는 게 전부고, LLM 자체는 stateless한 블랙박스다. 대화가 이어지는 건 우리가 만든 환상이다.
Simon Willison의 정의에 따르면 agent는 (1) 루프 안에서 돌아가는 LLM + (2) 도구 사용, 이 두 가지를 만족해야 한다. 도구 정의도 JSON 스키마 하나로 끝나서 추가하기 매우 쉽다.
예제에서 ping 같은 시스템 명령을 tool로 정의해서 LLM이 '이 호스트에 ping 쳐줘'라고 판단하면 실제로 subprocess를 실행하는 방식을 보여준다. tool calling의 구조가 직관적이다.
system prompt로 성격을 바꾸는 것도 간단하다. 예제에서 '진실만 말하는 Alph'와 '거짓만 말하는 Ralph' 두 context를 랜덤으로 전환하는 다중 성격 agent를 몇 줄로 구현했다.
글의 핵심 주장은 agent를 좋아하든 싫어하든, 직접 만들어봐야 제대로 판단할 수 있다는 것. 자전거 타기처럼 머리로만 이해할 수 없는 기술이라는 비유를 든다.
GPT-5를 예제에 사용했지만, OpenAI 호환 API(OpenRouter 등)를 쓰면 모델과 프로바이더를 런타임에 자유롭게 교체할 수 있다. 인터페이스가 사실상 업계 표준이 됐다.
howToApply: LLM agent 도입을 검토 중이라면, 글의 15줄 예제를 그대로 따라 치고 tool 하나(파일 읽기, DB 쿼리 등)를 붙여보면 agent의 실제 동작 원리와 한계를 30분 안에 체감할 수 있다.
이미 OpenAI API를 쓰고 있다면 OpenRouter를 연결해서 모델을 런타임에 교체하는 구조로 바꾸면, 비용이 민감한 작업에는 저렴한 모델, 정확도가 필요한 작업에는 frontier 모델을 쓰는 식으로 최적화할 수 있다.
사내 반복 작업(로그 분석, 배포 상태 확인 등)을 agent로 자동화할 때, tool을 UNIX 철학처럼 '한 가지만 잘하는' 단위로 쪼개면 보안 측면에서도 유리하고 디버깅도 쉬워진다.
agent 디버깅이 어렵다는 점을 감안해서, 각 tool call의 입출력을 로깅하고 step별로 재현할 수 있는 구조를 처음부터 설계해두면 '확률적 실패'에 대응하기 훨씬 수월하다.

en.oneLinerEn: LLM agents are surprisingly simple to implement with minimal code, but a hands-on approach is crucial to truly understand their mechanics and make informed decisions about their application.
en.targetAudienceEn: Developers conceptually familiar with LLM agents but lacking practical implementation experience, particularly those evaluating whether to adopt agent technology.
keyFindingsEn: The core of an LLM agent is remarkably simple: managing a context list alongside a single OpenAI API call can create a ChatGPT-like conversational app in under 15 lines of code.

The often-complex 'context window' is simply a list of strings. The entire process involves stacking user input and LLM responses into this list and sending it wholesale, while the LLM itself remains a stateless black box – the illusion of continuity is ours to create.
Following Simon Willison’s definition, an agent requires (1) an LLM running in a loop + (2) tool use, both of which are easily defined – tool definitions can be achieved with a single JSON schema.

The example demonstrates defining system commands like 'ping' as tools, allowing the LLM to trigger actual subprocess execution when it determines 'ping this host'. This showcases the intuitive structure of tool calling.

Changing an agent’s personality via system prompts is straightforward. The example implements a multi-personality agent with 'Alph' (truthful) and 'Ralph' (lying) contexts, randomly toggled in just a few lines of code.

The central argument is that hands-on implementation is essential for properly evaluating agents, regardless of one’s opinion. The author draws a parallel to learning to ride a bike – a skill that cannot be understood through theory alone.

While GPT-5 is used in the example, the use of OpenAI-compatible APIs (like OpenRouter) allows for runtime flexibility in model and provider selection, effectively making the interface an industry standard.
evidenceEn: One contributor shared their experience building an agent with 25 lines of PHP two years ago, which still functioned well with GPT-3.5. The perspective of viewing LLMs as UNIX text processing tools like 'sed' or 'awk' resonated with many, enabling natural application of composition, loops, and branching.

A realistic counterpoint was raised: 'Building it yourself is fun, but nobody likes debugging.' The initial experience can feel magical, but encountering failures at step 17, dealing with probabilistic and unreproducible results, and waiting 10-20 minutes to confirm a failure can be frustrating.

Some expressed skepticism, questioning why one should help improve a tool that could ultimately replace developers. Concerns were raised about the viability of agent-based projects given the unsustainable, loss-leading operation of many AI providers.

Analysis pointed out that while the OpenAI API neatly encapsulates tool calling, it fundamentally relies on instructing the LLM via prompt to use available tools and respond in a specific format when desired. This obscures the fact that everything boils down to token input and output.

Experiences were shared of building and iteratively improving coding agents. Utilizing fast inference services like Cerebras significantly improved multi-turn tool calls, and features like memory and speech transcription could be added in minutes.
howToApplyEn: If you're considering adopting LLM agents, replicate the 15-line example from the article and attach a single tool (file reading, database query, etc.) to quickly grasp the agent’s mechanics and limitations within 30 minutes.

If you’re already using the OpenAI API, integrate OpenRouter to enable runtime model switching. This allows for optimization by using cheaper models for cost-sensitive tasks and frontier models where accuracy is paramount.

When automating internal repetitive tasks (log analysis, deployment status checks) with agents, break down tools into small, single-purpose units, mirroring the UNIX philosophy. This enhances security and simplifies debugging.

Given the challenges of agent debugging, design your system from the outset to log the input and output of each tool call and enable step-by-step reproduction. This will significantly ease the handling of 'probabilistic failures'.

title: We pwned X, Vercel, Cursor, and Discord through a supply-chain attack

ko.oneLiner: AI 문서 플랫폼 Mintlify는 엔드포인트 검증 미흡으로 고객사 도메인(discord.com, docs.x.com 등)에서 악성 JavaScript를 실행할 수 있는 XSS 취약점을 초래했다.
keyFindings: Mintlify는 AI 기반 문서 플랫폼으로, 고객사가 자체 도메인(discord.com, docs.x.com 등)에서 Mintlify를 프록시해서 사용한다. 모든 Mintlify 사이트에는 내부 기능용 /_mintlify/* 경로가 존재하는데, 이 경로가 문제의 시작점이었다.
/_mintlify/static/[subdomain]/[파일경로] 엔드포인트가 요청한 subdomain이 현재 호스트와 일치하는지 검증하지 않았다. 즉, discord.com에서 공격자의 Mintlify 문서에 올린 파일을 그대로 가져올 수 있었다.

대부분의 파일 타입은 차단됐지만 SVG 파일은 통과했다. SVG에는 JavaScript를 삽입할 수 있고, 브라우저에서 직접 열면 스크립트가 실행된다. 공격자가 자기 Mintlify 문서에 악성 SVG를 올린 뒤 discord.com/_mintlify/static/evil/payload.svg 같은 URL로 접근하면, discord.com 오리진에서 JS가 실행되는 것.
이 XSS가 discord.com 오리진에서 실행되므로 Discord 세션 쿠키 탈취, 개발자 애플리케이션/웹훅 조작, Discord API를 통한 서버 삭제·DM 전송, 심지어 저장된 결제 정보로 Nitro 구매까지 가능했다.
영향 범위가 Mintlify를 사용하는 거의 모든 고객사로 확대됐다. X(Twitter), Vercel, Cursor, Discord 등 수백 개 기업이 포함된다. 하나의 SaaS 취약점이 모든 고객사에 전파되는 전형적인 공급망 공격 패턴.
Discord는 제보 후 2시간 만에 개발자 문서를 내리고 레거시 플랫폼으로 롤백했다. 바운티는 Discord $4,000, Mintlify 측 합산 약 $11,000 수준으로, 커뮤니티에서는 피해 규모 대비 너무 적다는 비판이 많았다.
공동 연구자 Eva가 발견한 별도 취약점에서는 Mintlify 서버 자체에서 RCE(원격 코드 실행)까지 가능했다. Node.js의 코드 생성 함수(eval 류)가 제대로 제한되지 않은 것이 원인.
발견자는 16세 고등학생으로, Discord 버그 바운티 리더보드 1위에 올라있으며 약 100건의 취약점을 제보한 경력이 있다.
howToApply: 자사 도메인에서 서드파티 SaaS를 프록시할 때는 반드시 별도 서브도메인(예: docs.example.com)을 사용하고, 메인 도메인(example.com)의 쿠키가 공유되지 않도록 도메인을 분리해라. 쿠키의 Domain 속성과 SameSite 설정도 점검.
CSP(Content Security Policy) 헤더에서 script-src를 엄격하게 설정해서, 인라인 스크립트와 SVG 내 스크립트 실행을 차단해라. 특히 서드파티 콘텐츠를 서빙하는 경로에는 sandbox CSP를 적용하는 것이 효과적.
사용자 업로드나 외부 소스의 SVG 파일을 서빙할 때는 Content-Type을 image/svg+xml 대신 Content-Disposition: attachment로 강제하거나, SVG를 래스터 이미지(PNG)로 변환해서 제공하는 방식을 고려해라.
Node.js 서버를 운영한다면 --disallow-code-generation-from-strings 플래그를 기본으로 적용해서 eval(), new Function() 등을 통한 RCE 벡터를 원천 차단해라.

en.oneLinerEn: A Mintlify AI document platform vulnerability allowed attackers to execute malicious JavaScript on customer domains like discord.com and docs.x.com due to insufficient endpoint validation. The flaw stemmed from an open /_mintlify/* path.
en.targetAudienceEn: Frontend/infrastructure engineers who proxy or embed third-party SaaS (document platforms, widgets, etc.) on their domains, and security developers responsible for managing Content Security Policy (CSP) settings.
keyFindingsEn: Mintlify is an AI-powered document platform where customers proxy it on their own domains (discord.com, docs.x.com, etc.). All Mintlify sites have an internal feature path, /_mintlify/*, which was the root cause of the issue.

The /_mintlify/static/[subdomain]/[filepath] endpoint failed to validate if the requested subdomain matched the current host. This allowed attackers to retrieve files uploaded to an attacker's Mintlify document directly from discord.com.

While most file types were blocked, SVG files were allowed. SVGs can contain JavaScript, which executes when opened directly in a browser. An attacker could upload a malicious SVG to their Mintlify document and access it via a URL like discord.com/_mintlify/static/evil/payload.svg, resulting in JS execution within the discord.com origin.

Because this XSS executed within the discord.com origin, it enabled attackers to steal Discord session cookies, manipulate developer applications/webhooks, delete servers and send DMs via the Discord API, and even purchase Nitro with stored payment information.

The impact extended to nearly all Mintlify customers, including hundreds of companies like X (Twitter), Vercel, Cursor, and Discord. This represents a typical supply chain attack pattern where a single SaaS vulnerability propagates to all customers.

Discord took down its developer documentation and rolled back to a legacy platform within two hours of being notified. The combined bounty from Discord ($4,000) and Mintlify (approximately $11,000) was widely criticized by the community as insufficient given the potential damage.

A separate vulnerability discovered by researcher Eva allowed for Remote Code Execution (RCE) on the Mintlify server itself, stemming from improperly restricted code generation functions (like eval) in Node.js.
The vulnerability was discovered by a 16-year-old high school student who is currently ranked #1 on the Discord bug bounty leaderboard and has reported approximately 100 vulnerabilities.
evidenceEn: Many argued the $4,000 bounty was absurd considering the potential for session cookie theft, account takeover, developer app manipulation, and payment information abuse when executing JS within the discord.com origin – all triggered by a single link click.

Critics stated, "A VC-backed AI startup securing enterprise customers without proper security validation, unable to prevent basic XSS." Mintlify published a complex caching architecture blog post, but lacked fundamental security practices.

From an infrastructure perspective, advice surfaced stating, "Proxying third-party services directly on a core domain (discord.com) is always a bad idea. Using a separate subdomain like dev-docs.discord.com with a CNAME record would have limited the blast radius."

Reports surfaced 38 days after public disclosure indicating the attack surface was being exploited by phishing infrastructure, including 101 URLs matching the pattern discord.flawing.top/blog/* and 20 phishing URLs on openopenbox301.vercel.app, totaling 121 IOCs.
Some argued that allowing scripts within SVG files was a design flaw in itself, as most messaging platforms like Discord, Facebook Messenger, and Google Hangouts block SVG uploads or previews.
howToApplyEn: When proxying third-party SaaS on your domain, always use a separate subdomain (e.g., docs.example.com) and isolate the main domain (example.com) to prevent cookie sharing. Review the Domain attribute and SameSite settings of your cookies.

Strictly configure the script-src directive in your Content Security Policy (CSP) header to block inline scripts and script execution within SVGs. Applying a sandbox CSP to paths serving third-party content is effective.
When serving user-uploaded or external SVG files, consider forcing the Content-Type to image/svg+xml with Content-Disposition: attachment, or converting SVGs to raster images (PNG).
If operating a Node.js server, apply the --disallow-code-generation-from-strings flag by default to prevent RCE vectors through eval(), new Function(), and similar functions.

title: DS$^2$-Instruct: Domain-Specific Data Synthesis for Large Language Models Instruction Tuning

ko.oneLiner: 프레임워크는 태스크 정의만 입력받아 금융·의학·수학 등 전문 도메인 파인튜닝 데이터를 인간 개입 없이 자동으로 생성한다.
keyFindings: 태스크 설명(task definition)만 있으면 seed 데이터나 도메인 문서 없이 zero-shot으로 instruction 데이터셋 생성 가능
키워드를 기초 개념(prerequisite)과 심화 개념(advanced) 양방향으로 확장하고, BM25로 The Pile 문서를 검색해 키워드 풀을 보강함
Bloom's Taxonomy(기억→이해→적용→분석→평가→창조 6단계 인지 수준 분류 체계)를 적용해 단순 암기 문제부터 창의적 문제까지 다양한 난이도의 질문 자동 생성
Self-consistency filtering(같은 질문에 여러 번 답변 생성해서 일관성 높은 것만 남기는 품질 필터)으로 애매하거나 잘못된 instruction-response 쌍 자동 제거
Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct로 데이터 생성 후 Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B, Qwen2.5-7B에 LoRA(파라미터 일부만 학습하는 경량 파인튜닝 기법)로 파인튜닝해서 7개 도메인 벤치마크 전반에서 기존 방법 대비 일관되게 성능 향상
데이터 6,000개 기준에서도 성능 곡선이 포화되지 않아서 더 많은 데이터로 추가 개선 여지 있음
howToApply: 도메인 특화 LLM을 만들어야 할 때, 태스크 설명 텍스트 하나를 작성하고 DS²-INSTRUCT 파이프라인을 돌려 수천 개의 instruction-response 쌍을 생성한 뒤 LoRA(r=8, α=16)로 파인튜닝하면 됨. 어노테이터 없이도 됨.
키워드 생성 단계에서 50개 시드 키워드 → 100회 양방향 확장 → BM25 검색 보강 순서로 진행하면 도메인 커버리지가 크게 넓어짐. 소규모 도메인이라면 이터레이션 수를 줄여도 무방.
Self-consistency 필터링 threshold를 τ=3/5(5번 중 3번 이상 같은 답)으로 설정하면 노이즈 데이터를 자동 제거할 수 있음. 정확도가 중요한 의료·금융 도메인일수록 threshold를 높이면 품질 ↑, 데이터 양 ↓ 트레이드오프를 조절 가능.

en.oneLinerEn: This framework automatically generates fine-tuning data for specialized domains like finance, medicine, and mathematics, requiring only task definitions and eliminating the need for human intervention.
en.targetAudienceEn: ML engineers needing to fine-tune LLMs for specific domains such as law, healthcare, and finance, or teams developing domain-specific chatbots. This is particularly useful for developers facing a lack of training data or difficulty sourcing expert annotators.
keyFindingsEn: Instruction datasets can be generated zero-shot from task definitions alone, without requiring seed data or domain documents.
Keywords are expanded bidirectionally into both prerequisite and advanced concepts, and the keyword pool is enriched by searching The Pile corpus using BM25.

Bloom's Taxonomy (a six-level cognitive classification system ranging from remembering to creating) is applied to automatically generate questions of varying difficulty, from simple memorization to creative problem-solving.

Self-consistency filtering (a quality filter that retains only consistent responses from multiple generations of the same question) automatically removes ambiguous or incorrect instruction-response pairs.

After generating data with Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct, fine-tuning Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B, and Qwen2.5-7B with LoRA consistently improved performance across seven domain benchmarks compared to existing methods.
The performance curve does not saturate with 6,000 data points, indicating potential for further improvement with more data.
evidenceEn: On Llama-3.1-8B, the zero-shot average increased from 14.34% to 42.83% after DS²-INSTRUCT fine-tuning, a roughly 3x improvement, and +16.89%p compared to the previous state-of-the-art (InstructMix 25.94%).
On Mistral-7B, the zero-shot average increased from 9.70% to 37.83% after DS²-INSTRUCT fine-tuning, and +7.54%p compared to the previous best (InstructMix 30.29%).
On Qwen2.5-7B, DS²-INSTRUCT achieved an average of 54.95%, +1.88%p compared to the previous best (InstructMix 53.07%), ranking first in all seven domains.
Data quality evaluation (manual review of 500 samples): 96.83% valid instructions, 91.26% valid responses, and 94.91% domain relevance on GSM8K.
howToApplyEn: To create a domain-specific LLM, write a single task description and run the DS²-INSTRUCT pipeline to generate thousands of instruction-response pairs, then fine-tune with LoRA (r=8, α=16). No annotators are required.

The keyword generation process should follow the sequence of 50 seed keywords → 100 bidirectional expansions → BM25 search enhancement to significantly broaden domain coverage. For smaller domains, the number of iterations can be reduced.

Setting the self-consistency filtering threshold to τ=3/5 (at least 3 out of 5 answers are the same) can automatically remove noisy data. For high-accuracy domains like healthcare and finance, increasing the threshold allows for a trade-off between quality and data quantity.

title: I stopped using Claude.ai entirely. I run my entire business through Claude Code.

ko.oneLiner: Claude Code가 CRM·콘텐츠 파이프라인·리드소싱을 구동하며 Claude.ai 웹앱을 완전히 대체해 전체 비즈니스를 단일 플랫폼으로 운영하게 했다.
keyFindings: 코딩뿐 아니라 CRM·콘텐츠·영업 파이프라인을 모두 Claude Code 터미널에서 처리
아침 커맨드 하나로 하루 전체 업무 레이아웃 자동 생성
Claude를 대화 상대가 아닌 비즈니스 인프라로 취급하는 패러다임 전환
howToApply: 반복 업무를 Claude Code 커맨드로 추상화해 아침 루틴에 통합
좋은 CLAUDE.md + README.md 조합이 핵심

keyFindingsEn: Handle coding, CRM, content, and sales pipelines all within the Claude Code terminal.
Automatically generate a full day's work layout with a single morning command.

evidenceEn: Currently processing CRM, content, and sales pipelines all within the Claude Code terminal.
Automatically generate a full day's work layout with a single morning command.
Community validation confirms that a strong CLAUDE.md + README.md combination is key.
